<description>
`LoadWalletFlags` checks for `WALLET_FLAG_DESCRIPTORS` only inside `if (batch.Read(DBKeys::FLAGS, flags))`. A SQLite wallet file without a FLAGS record is loaded with no flags set and then handled as a legacy wallet, which ends in an `Assert`:

- with a legacy record in the file: `SetupLegacyDataSPKM`, `Assert(m_database->Format() == "bdb_ro" || m_database->Format() == "sqlite-mock")`
- without one: `LoadActiveScriptPubKeyMan`, `Assert(IsWalletFlagSet(WALLET_FLAG_DESCRIPTORS))`

`loadwallet` on such a file aborts the node. If the wallet is in the load on startup list, the node aborts on every start. The existing check for legacy records in a descriptor wallet (`UNEXPECTED_LEGACY_ENTRY`) does not catch this, because it also depends on the flag.

The second commit does the check whether or not the record exists, so the file is rejected with the legacy wallet error.

The first commit is needed for that: `bitcoin-wallet create` opened the new, empty database through `PopulateWalletFromDB` before it wrote the flags, which is the case the comment "The FLAGS key is absent during wallet creation" refers to. `CWallet::CreateNew` does not load anymore, and now the tool does not either. It writes the version records itself, as `CreateNew` does.

**Behavior change:** a wallet database without a FLAGS record no longer loads. `bitcoin-wallet create` writes the same set of records as before (compared by record type on a new wallet).

**Measurement:** regtest, RelWithDebInfo, base a527a0077a, descriptor wallet made with `createwallet`, then edited with sqlite3.

| file | master | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FLAGS record deleted | node aborts, `wallet.cpp:3577` | error -4, node keeps running |
| FLAGS record deleted, `cscript` record added | node aborts, `wallet.cpp:3404` | error -4, node keeps running |
| unchanged | loads | loads |

**Tests:** new case in `wallet_descriptor.py` for both files; on master the node aborts in it. Three unit tests that load a hand written database now write the flags first. Passing locally: `test_bitcoin` and `test_runner.py` with the default list. Not run: fuzz targets, lint.

Contributed by [turingpoint](https://www.turingpoint.de).
</description>

<commits>
94787f83f6 wallettool: Do not load a newly created wallet database

The create command opened the new, empty database through
PopulateWalletFromDB before it set the wallet flags and generated the
descriptors. There is nothing to load at that point, and it made the
loading code accept a database without a FLAGS record.

Skip the load when creating, and write the version records in
WalletCreate as CWallet::CreateNew does, since loading no longer
writes them.

Signed-off-by: Jan Kahmen <jan@turingpoint.de>

7af8fcd6fb wallet: Require the descriptors flag when the FLAGS record is missing

LoadWalletFlags only checked for WALLET_FLAG_DESCRIPTORS when the
database had a FLAGS record. A SQLite wallet file without that record
was loaded with no flags set and then handled as a legacy wallet,
which ends in an Assert:

- with a legacy record, in SetupLegacyDataSPKM, because the database
  is not bdb_ro
- otherwise in LoadActiveScriptPubKeyMan, because the descriptors
  flag is not set

loadwallet aborts the node on such a file, and with the wallet in the
load on startup list the node no longer starts.

Do the check whether or not the record exists, so the file is
rejected as a legacy wallet. Nothing loads a database without the
record anymore now that the wallet tool does not load on create. The
unit tests that load a hand written database write the flags first.

Signed-off-by: Jan Kahmen <jan@turingpoint.de>
</commits>
